siguiri-area-one.conditions_add: The condition documented for IFC's money is placed on the bank, not on AngloGold Ashanti or its Guinean subsidiary. IFC's summary of its subordinated Tier II loan of up to ZAR 1 billion (about US$139 million) to Nedbank (project 26014, approved 24 May 2007, signed 2 July 2007), which was to support black economic empowerment financing, affordable housing finance and cross-border corporate lending across Africa, says the bank was to develop or upgrade, if necessary, its Social and Environmental Management System before disbursement to IFC's satisfaction, to name responsible, qualified people to manage and implement it, to commit to implementing it so that its activities comply with the applicable requirements, and to submit a periodic report to IFC as per a format to be provided by IFC. The loan was classified Category FI. IFC's own Compliance Advisor Ombudsman registered the 2017 complaint about the 2015 resettlement of Area One against this same project 26014, naming AngloGold Ashanti as a Nedbank client and its Guinean subsidiary SAG as "IFC's sub-client" (IFC, Summary of Proposed Investment, project 26014; CAO, Guinea: NedBank Tier II-01/Kintinian).

hagl-ratanakiri.conditions_add: The condition documented for IFC's money is placed on the fund, not on HAGL. The IFC investment through which IFC was exposed to Hoang Anh Gia Lai is VEIL II: CAO's assessment report is headed "CAO Assessment Report Regarding IFC's VEIL II Project (20926)", records that "IFC's investment into the Fund was made in several disbursements for a total of US$16.4 million" for 5.5 per cent of the fund, and says "One of the beneficiaries of the Fund is Hoang Anh Gia Lai known as HAGL". IFC's summary of that investment (project 20926, the lower of US$8 million or 20 per cent of the capital increase, approved 11 June 2003, signed 20 June 2003, invested 24 October 2003) carries one environmental requirement: VEIL will be required to demonstrate that the existing environmental management system is still in place. The earlier IFC investment in VEIL and Dragon Capital Group (project 10740, up to US$12 million, signed 3 December 2001), which does require the manager to obtain IFC clearance before investing IFC funds in any Category A project, is a separate and earlier investment and is not the one CAO ties to HAGL (IFC, Summary of Proposed Investment, project 20926; CAO, Assessment Report, VEIL II (20926), May 2014).

green-resources-uganda-evictions.conditions_add: IFC's environmental and social review summary for its Green Resources investment (project 26506, approved 20 April 2009, signed 1 May 2009) attaches an Environmental Action Plan dated 10 March 2008 and sets out what the companies were to do. Sao Hill Industries, the Tanzanian sawmill, was to commence activities to fully institutionalize an integrated management system covering environment, social, quality and occupational health and safety, to phase out the use of CCA for treatment of sawn lumber, to prepare the emergency preparedness and response plan it lacked, and to carry out the environmental evaluations needed to obtain its facility permits; Green Resources was to improve assessments and implementation activities in accordance with the action plan. On land the summary records that the plantations sit on land leased from the government for 99 years and that it is Green Resources company policy to avoid using land that entails either physical or economic dislocation - the company's own policy, not an IFC requirement. The summary names the Kachung plantation in Uganda only in connection with expected FSC and CDM certification, and does not mention Bukaleba (IFC, Environmental and Social Review Summary, project 26506).

why.safeguard: carry out the environmental evaluations needed to obtain its facility permits
why.admin: commence activities to fully institutionalize an integrated management system

mozal-bypass.conditions_add: IFC's summary for the Mozal II expansion (project 10323, a US$25 million IFC loan for its own account within a US$992 million project financed with US$600 million of loans, approved 12 April 2001, signed 29 June 2001) sets out reporting and disclosure requirements attached to the financing. Annual environmental monitoring reports were required, measuring performance against the environmental and social requirements, host-country regulation and any requirements in the investment agreement, and the monitoring report had to be completed or verified for completeness and accuracy by an independent consultant acceptable to IFC. The sponsor had to notify stakeholders publicly and make the draft environmental impact assessment available locally no later than 60 days before the proposed board date, and a preliminary public consultation and disclosure plan was submitted to IFC's environment and social review unit for review and approval. The project was rated Category A (IFC, Summary of Proposed Investment, project 10323).

ixquisis-hydro-guatemala.conditions_add: IDB Invest's environmental and social review for Generadora San Mateo, the 20 MW San Mateo plant, states: "The Company will be required to carry out the actions included in the Environmental and Social Action Plan (ESAP)." The company also had to submit regular progress reports on that plan to the IIC. Because the transmission line crosses an internationally recognised key biodiversity area, the review states that the IIC will require the project to comply with the applicable requirements of IFC Performance Standard 6. The plan's items include completing a supplemental environmental impact assessment with a critical habitat assessment, expanding the biological baseline along the transmission corridor, assessing how communities use river snails, shrimp and crabs, monitoring minimum ecological flows of 750 litres a second on the Pojom river and 300 on the Negro river, and setting up a grievance mechanism for workers and affected people. The parallel review for Generadora San Andres, the 10.65 MW plant, sets the same action plan requirement, with minimum flows of 140 litres a second on the Primavera, 100 on the Varsovia and 80 on the Palmira. On land, the San Mateo review records that the parcels were purchased through direct negotiations with the landowners and that no land was acquired through eminent domain or other government action (IDB Invest, Environmental and Social Review, Generadora San Mateo and Generadora San Andres).

amaravati-land-pooling.conditions_add: The money that was actually committed is the Asian Development Bank's. Its November 2024 report and recommendation of the President for the Amaravati Integrated Urban Development Program ties a loan of 121,972,000,000 yen (US$788.80 million equivalent) to eight disbursement-linked indicators, states that the program excludes high-risk activities, including the physical displacement of people living in village clusters, and sets a program action plan item to conduct a social audit of the land assembly process and livelihood impacts at program baseline, midterm and end-term. The World Bank's requirements for the earlier Amaravati Sustainable Infrastructure and Institutional Development Project (P159808) belonged to a proposed US$300 million loan, within a US$715 million project, that was never approved - India withdrew the request in July 2019 - so they bound no one: its project information document and integrated safeguards data sheet said the Bank's involuntary resettlement policy will be applicable to all lands that are assembled for the project, that the Resettlement Policy Framework is part of legal agreements, set a cut-off date of 8 December 2014 for non-titleholders, recorded that the increased land pooling payments for 2016-18 would be paid retroactively after loan approval, and would have required an Environmental and Social Management Framework for this Category A project, project-specific assessment by an independent agency for E1 subcomponents, independent consultants for concurrent monitoring of resettlement, and evidence that three dedicated staff were in place prior to appraisal (ADB, Report and Recommendation of the President, 2024; World Bank, Project Information Document/Integrated Safeguards Data Sheet, 2019).

sudan-2013-fuel-subsidy.conditions_add: No IMF money carried these measures. The IMF's engagement with Sudan in this period was an Article IV consultation, which is surveillance, and then a staff-monitored programme that the IMF's Managing Director approved on 27 March 2014, six months after the September 2013 protests, covering January to December 2014. The IMF's press release announcing that programme states that staff-monitored programmes do not entail financial assistance or endorsement by the IMF Executive Board, with progress tracked through quantitative targets and structural benchmarks; it names no loan or disbursement and does not mention fuel subsidies. Sudan was also in arrears to the IMF and cleared them only on 29 June 2021, so there was no IMF credit in 2013 for a condition to attach to (IMF, Press Release No. 14/139, 27 March 2014; IMF, Frequently Asked Questions on Sudan).

Before the first disbursement the concessionaire had to deliver a water efficiency programme with a construction-phase water consumption estimate, a fauna management protocol adjusted for species distribution and biological corridors, and updated land plans: a sociopredial management plan, a land acquisition plan, a socioeconomic compensation plan and a socioeconomic follow-up plan. An emergency response and spill prevention plan for operation was due 90 days before construction ended, and a resettlement audit focused on vulnerable families two years after it ended (IDB Invest, Environmental and Social Review Summary, Ruta del Cacao).
